code_quality.reasoning: The reference patch is limited to two production files, uses the existing in-place normalization style, introduces no dead declarations, and has no visible violation of the repository ESLint configuration (`eslint.config.mjs:1-15`). Its early budget return nevertheless bypasses an established safety invariant: it no longer removes `cache_control` from a `defer_loading` tool when the request already has four markers, despite the existing code and regression test documenting that <provider> rejects that combination. That regression makes the guard too blunt for a maintainer-ready change.

issues.detail: Do not use `countCacheControlBlocks(body) >= 4` as an unconditional return. For example, a native Claude body with five alternating user/assistant messages, each containing an array with one text block carrying `cache_control`, is unaffected by bare-object normalization; the counter is five and the new return leaves all five markers in place. Since `chatCore` invokes `anchorClaudeCache` immediately before dispatch for native Claude passthrough, that invalid body reaches the Claude endpoint. Preserve the no-reanchor behavior at exactly four if desired, but prune/re-anchor an over-budget body so the final count is at most four.
issues.evidence: The description promises: "a request delivered to a Claude endpoint must never carry more than four cache_control markers." The patched early return in `open-sse/translator/formats/claude.js` is in `anchorClaudeCache` (the function starts at base line 272), and the native dispatch path calls it at `open-sse/handlers/chatCore.js:302`.
issues.title: Requests already carrying more than four markers are forwarded unchanged

issues.detail: Move bare-content normalization ahead of the `role: system` branch in `convertClaudeMessage` (and remove the marker there), or make `systemReminderText` accept a single block. With `{ role: "system", content: { type: "text", text: "keep this" } }`, the current early branch calls `systemReminderText` before the newly added wrapper. That helper accepts only strings or arrays, returns an empty string for the object, and the converter returns `null`, dropping the entire message.
issues.evidence: The description requires that a single-block turn be kept for "requests translated from Claude format into <provider> format." `open-sse/translator/request/claude-to-<provider>.js:134-151` shows `systemReminderText` rejecting object content and `convertClaudeMessage` returning for `ROLE.SYSTEM` before reaching the patch's subsequently added normalization.
issues.title: Bare-object mid-conversation system messages are still lost on the Claude-to-<provider> leg

issues.detail: Retain validation/cleanup of invalid cache placements even when no new anchor can be added. A body with four direct markers, one on `{ defer_loading: true, cache_control: ... }`, now hits the new count guard and never reaches the existing tools loop that deletes the marker from every non-selected tool. Strip the deferred-tool marker first, then decide whether there is budget to anchor; this preserves the pre-existing upstream-safety guarantee.
issues.evidence: `tests/unit/defer-loading-cache-control.test.js:3-15` documents <provider>'s rejection of a tool that combines `defer_loading: true` and `cache_control`; base `open-sse/translator/formats/claude.js:284-290` enforces that by clearing non-selected tool markers. The patch's new early return is before that cleanup.
issues.title: The full-budget guard regresses deferred-tool cache safety

evaluation.overall_feedback:
The reference solution touches two files, both production code: `open-sse/translator/formats/claude.js` and `open-sse/translator/request/claude-to-<provider>.js`. It changes no tests, documentation, generated files, or configuration. The normalization work is otherwise sensibly placed for the ordinary target-Claude and native-passthrough paths: it wraps bare content before filtering/folding and removes the bare block's client cache marker without disturbing pre-existing arrays.

The marker-budget check needs to enforce a cap, not merely avoid adding another marker when the count is already high. In particular, distinguish exactly-four (where retaining client anchors may be appropriate) from over-four, and retain existing invalid-placement cleanup such as the deferred-tool rule. Also normalize before every consumer of `msg.content` in the Claude-to-<provider> converter; the system-message early return currently bypasses the new handling and loses a supported message form.

After those boundary paths are corrected, the implementation's small scope and use of existing cache-anchor conventions would be a solid fit for this codebase.

solution_comprehensiveness.reasoning: The patch correctly handles the principal normal paths: `prepareClaudeRequest` normalizes a bare block before cache stripping/valid-content filtering, and native passthrough normalizes before system-message folding; the Claude→<provider> converter also handles bare non-system user/assistant blocks. However, `anchorClaudeCache` now returns unchanged for any count of four or more. Five otherwise valid, array-backed text blocks bearing `cache_control` therefore remain five markers and can be dispatched on the native Claude passthrough path (`chatCore.js:302`), directly contradicting the unconditional four-marker limit. In addition, the new Claude→<provider> normalization is placed after the early return for `role: system`, so a bare-object mid-conversation system message is still discarded rather than preserved.

evaluation.summary: Bare content handling is substantially improved, but over-budget marker requests and bare system turns still violate the promised end-to-end behavior.

summary: Bare content handling is substantially improved, but over-budget marker requests and bare system turns still violate the promised end-to-end behavior.
